questions.stem: The Indian Constitution provides for THREE types of Emergencies. Article 352 covers:
questions.explanation: THREE TYPES OF EMERGENCIES under Indian Constitution (Part XVIII, Articles 352-360): (1) ARTICLE 352 — NATIONAL EMERGENCY on grounds of WAR, EXTERNAL AGGRESSION, or ARMED REBELLION (44th Amend 1978 replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' to raise the bar). (2) ARTICLE 356 — STATE EMERGENCY / PRESIDENT'S RULE — 'failure of constitutional machinery in a state'. (3) ARTICLE 360 — FINANCIAL EMERGENCY — due to threat to financial stability of India. PROCLAIMED 3 TIMES so far nationally (Art 352): (a) 1962 Sino-Indian war (till 1968), (b) 1971 Indo-Pak War (till 1977), (c) 25 June 1975 — Indira Gandhi's INTERNAL EMERGENCY (for 21 months till 21 March 1977). Article 356 used 100+ times (controversial). Article 360 NEVER used (never proclaimed financial emergency). Borrowed from the WEIMAR CONSTITUTION (Germany). war, external aggression, armed rebellion.
questions.subject: Polity

_fixes.was: NATIONAL EMERGENCY (war, external aggression, armed rebellion)

questions.stem: The NATIONAL EMERGENCY (Art 352) can be proclaimed by the President only on the WRITTEN recommendation of:
questions.explanation: PROCEDURE for National Emergency (post-44th Amendment 1978 safeguards): (1) Proclamation by the President, ONLY upon WRITTEN recommendation of the UNION CABINET (the whole cabinet, not just PM — raised bar). (2) Must be APPROVED by BOTH Houses of Parliament within ONE MONTH by SPECIAL MAJORITY (2/3 of members present + voting AND majority of total membership). (3) Once approved, operates for 6 MONTHS; can be extended every 6 months with fresh parliamentary approval. (4) Can be REVOKED by the President at any time by subsequent proclamation. (5) LOK SABHA can pass a RESOLUTION disapproving → Emergency must be revoked (simple majority suffices for disapproval). These safeguards were introduced BECAUSE of abuses during Indira Gandhi's Emergency (1975-77) — PM had ADVISED Emergency single-handedly, without Cabinet consultation (called a Cabinet meeting only AFTER the proclamation was signed). President FAKHRUDDIN ALI AHMED famously signed at midnight 25 June 1975 — the 'darkest day' of Indian democracy per critics. as modified by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

_fixes.was: Union CABINET (as modified by the 44th Amendment, 1978)

questions.stem: During a National Emergency under Article 352, which Fundamental Rights can NEVER be suspended?

options.option_text: Articles 20 and 21 — Protection against double jeopardy/ex-post facto/self-incrimination + Right to Life & Personal Liberty (NEVER suspendable post-44th Amendment)

questions.explanation: Article 359 (as amended by 44th Amendment 1978): during National Emergency, President can suspend enforcement of any Fundamental Right EXCEPT Articles 20 and 21. (1) ART 20 — Protection: no ex-post facto law, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination. (2) ART 21 — Right to Life and Personal Liberty. These are NEVER suspendable. Art 19 rights (freedoms) — automatically suspended when Emergency declared on grounds of WAR or EXTERNAL AGGRESSION (restored post-Emergency); on grounds of ARMED REBELLION, they're NOT auto-suspended. Other FRs (14, 22, 25, 29, 32 etc.) — their enforcement can be suspended by Presidential order. WHY this SAFEGUARD for Arts 20 + 21: the 1975-77 Emergency saw the SC in ADM JABALPUR v. SHIVKANT SHUKLA (1976) rule 4-1 that even Art 21 (right to life) could be suspended (Justice HR Khanna's lone dissent — he was subsequently superseded for the CJI post). This SHAMEFUL decision was overturned by K.S. PUTTASWAMY v UNION (2017) — Right to Privacy case. 44th Amendment specifically amended Art 359 to prevent such suspensions again. Also 44th made it clear mere declaration of Emergency doesn't auto-suspend FRs — need specific Presidential order per Art 359.

questions.stem: PRESIDENT'S RULE (Article 356) imposes direct Central rule on a state. Maximum duration:
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 356 — President's Rule / 'State Emergency' imposed when 'the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution'. Grounds: no party has majority, coalition collapses, CM-Governor rift, constitutional breakdown. PROCEDURE: Proclamation by President based on REPORT from GOVERNOR. Must be approved by BOTH Houses of Parliament (SIMPLE MAJORITY) within 2 MONTHS. Once approved, operates for 6 MONTHS. EXTENDABLE with parliamentary approval every 6 months, but MAX 3 YEARS total (Art 356(4)). Beyond 3 years requires specific conditions: emergency under Art 352 in force OR Election Commission certifies elections can't be held. Effects: (a) Governor runs the state on behalf of President; (b) Parliament assumes State Legislature functions; (c) State assembly may be dissolved. 100+ impositions since independence — often MISUSED politically. SARKARIA COMMISSION (1988) recommended restraint. S.R. BOMMAI v. UNION OF INDIA (1994) — landmark case — held Art 356 subject to JUDICIAL REVIEW; floor test of majority should be in Assembly, not Raj Bhavan; SC can strike down dismissals. Most recent: Uttarakhand 2016 (struck down by HC), Arunachal 2016 (struck down by SC). extendable up to 3 YEARS total (with conditions per Article 356(4) & (5)).

questions.stem: The INTERNAL EMERGENCY of 25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977 was proclaimed by:
questions.explanation: INTERNAL EMERGENCY — proclaimed on 25 June 1975 by PRESIDENT FAKHRUDDIN ALI AHMED (5th President, 1974-77) on the advice of PM INDIRA GANDHI. DURATION: 21 months (25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977). BACKGROUND: (1) 12 June 1975 — Allahabad HC (Justice Jagmohanlal Sinha) found Indira Gandhi GUILTY of electoral malpractice in Raj Narain v. Indira Gandhi case (Rae Bareli 1971 election), set aside her election, barred her from office for 6 years; (2) Opposition + JAYAPRAKASH NARAYAN called for her resignation, launched 'Sampoorna Kranti' (Total Revolution) movement — even exhorted police + army to disobey unconstitutional orders; (3) To stay in power, Indira advised Emergency on grounds of 'INTERNAL DISTURBANCE' — signed by Ahmed that night, Cabinet informed only next morning. FEATURES: press censorship, arrest of opposition leaders (Vajpayee, Advani, JP, Morarji Desai, Raj Narain), forced sterilisations under Sanjay Gandhi (Delhi slum demolitions at Turkman Gate), 20-point programme, 42nd Amendment passed with extensive changes. 1977 ELECTION: INDIRA lost — JANATA PARTY government (Morarji Desai 1st non-Congress PM). Janata passed 44th Amendment (1978) reversing major Emergency excesses. 'INDIAN DEMOCRACY'S DARKEST HOUR' — per many historians; but supporters argue it stabilised economy. on PM Indira Gandhi's advice.

questions.stem: Financial Emergency under Article 360 has been PROCLAIMED in India how many times since 1950?

options.option_text: NEVER — Article 360 has not been invoked even in 1991 BoP crisis

questions.explanation: FINANCIAL EMERGENCY (ART 360) — has NEVER BEEN PROCLAIMED in Indian history (as of 2026). Even during severe crises like the 1991 BoP crisis (India had reserves for just ~2 weeks of imports; gold pledged to Bank of England to raise $600 million), Art 360 was not invoked. Grounds for Art 360: 'threat to the financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof'. PROCEDURE: Presidential proclamation, approved by BOTH Houses of Parliament by simple majority within 2 months. Once approved, operates UNTIL REVOKED (no max duration — unusual feature). EFFECTS: (1) Union can give directions to States; (2) Salaries + allowances of State employees (including HC + SC judges) can be reduced; (3) Money bills + financial bills may be reserved for Presidential consideration. Article 360 is viewed as a LAST RESORT — invoking it signals international financial distress + could trigger loss of sovereign rating, capital flight. COMPARATIVE: US uses Federal Reserve tools + Congress; many countries have defaulted (Argentina, Sri Lanka 2022, etc.) without invoking a similar clause. 1991 India TACKLED via IMF loan + structural adjustment programme (Manmohan Singh as FM, LPG reforms) — WITHOUT a formal Art 360.

questions.stem: The concept of Emergency provisions in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from which country's constitution?
questions.explanation: EMERGENCY PROVISIONS in the Indian Constitution borrowed primarily from the WEIMAR CONSTITUTION of Germany (1919, Republic of Weimar between 1919-33). Weimar's Article 48 gave the President (Hindenburg) power to use emergency decrees — used extensively in the 1920s-30s, most infamously by Hitler to seize dictatorial power after 1933 Reichstag fire. This DARK HISTORY was fresh in Constituent Assembly members' minds when they debated Emergency provisions. Some, like H.V. Kamath, opposed these provisions as potentially dangerous. Dr. AMBEDKAR defended them: 'The Constitution as framed requires the presence of a strong Executive in the center, whenever needed to be able to preserve the stability of the country and unity of the federation.' He acknowledged the risk but argued safeguards (parliamentary approval + judicial review) would suffice. The 1975-77 Emergency VINDICATED the worst fears — Emergency WAS misused. 44th Amendment 1978 strengthened safeguards substantially. Emergency provisions in India are thus MORE ELABORATE than most democracies. 'PRESIDENT'S RULE' (Art 356) concept also has echo of central emergency provisions in the Gov of India Act 1935 (sec 93). 1919 Weimar Constitution.
